title: Path A — Foundations
subtitle: Networking, Linux, Core Security & Scripting
description: Start here with zero prior experience. Master how computers communicate, navigate the Linux operating system without a graphical interface, understand core defensive principles, and write introductory automation scripts.
prerequisites: A working computer (Windows, macOS, or Linux) with internet access
Curiosity about how systems and protocols operate under the hood

steps.title: Networking Fundamentals
steps.goal: Understand TCP/IP, OSI model, IP addressing, subnetting, switching, routing, DNS, and common protocol ports.
steps.resourceChoice: Choose either Jeremy's IT Lab (structured, lab-heavy with Packet Tracer) or NetworkChuck (high-energy, conceptual overview). You do not need to watch both in full.
steps.specialNote: Focus heavily on IPv4 subnetting and observing packet handshakes in packet analyzer tools.
checklist: Explain the difference between Layer 2 (MAC) and Layer 3 (IP) forwarding
Calculate usable host ranges and network IDs from CIDR notation (/24, /27, /30)
Identify well-known ports: 21, 22, 23, 25, 53, 80, 443, 445, 3389
Trace an end-to-end HTTP request through DNS resolution and TCP handshake

steps.title: Linux Fundamentals (Part 1 — Command Line)
steps.goal: Gain comfort inside the Linux command line terminal without relying on a graphical user interface.
steps.specialNote: Pair this directly with OverTheWire Bandit wargame levels 0 through 15.
checklist: Navigate the filesystem using cd, ls, pwd, and understand relative vs absolute paths
Create, copy, move, view, and remove files and directories with mkdir, cp, mv, cat, less, rm
Read system identification files such as /etc/os-release and uname -a
Complete OverTheWire Bandit levels 0 through 10 independently

steps.title: Linux Fundamentals (Part 2 — Permissions & Administration)
steps.goal: Master POSIX file permissions, user and group management, process control, and text manipulation tools.
checklist: Interpret octal and symbolic permissions (e.g. chmod 755 vs 600, chown)
Filter and search text streams using grep, find, awk, and cut
Inspect running processes and open network sockets using ps, top, and ss
Complete OverTheWire Bandit levels 11 through 20

steps.title: Core Security Principles
steps.goal: Establish foundational security mental models: CIA triad, threat modeling, defense in depth, and access control.
checklist: Differentiate between Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability with concrete examples
Explain the difference between Authentication (who you are) and Authorization (what you can do)
Understand the Principle of Least Privilege and Defense-in-Depth
Identify basic social engineering, phishing, and password hygiene risks

steps.title: Python for Security Automation
steps.goal: Learn core Python syntax (variables, loops, functions, lists, dicts) to build simple security utilities.
steps.specialNote: Approximately 4.5 hours of video. Follow with building small scripts for a personal lab, such as a log parser or hash checker.
checklist: Write a Python script that reads a text log file and counts occurrences of an IP address
Write a simple port banner grabber using the python standard socket library
Generate SHA-256 hashes of files to verify data integrity
Execute scripts from the terminal with command-line arguments

title: Path B — Security+ Certification Track
subtitle: CompTIA SY0-701 Exam Objectives & Applied Cryptography
description: Structured curriculum mapped directly to the CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 examination. Gain thorough technical grounding in threats, attacks, architecture, incident response, and applied cryptography.
prerequisites: Path A (Foundations) or equivalent networking and Linux fundamentals
versionNotice: This course covers exam SY0-701. The English SY0-701 exam retires on 11 June 2027. The new SY0-801 exam launches around 17 Nov 2026. Check CompTIA's official page for the latest.
versionNoticeVerified: Verified against CompTIA official lifecycle announcement (November 2026). Note: Watching video courses alone does not grant certification; verify official exam voucher and scheduling requirements with CompTIA.

steps.title: CompTIA SY0-701 Complete Video Course
steps.goal: Complete the full video syllabus covering all five CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 domains.
checklist: Domain 1.0: General Security Concepts (12%)
Domain 2.0: Threats, Vulnerabilities, and Mitigations (22%)
Domain 3.0: Security Architecture (18%)
Domain 4.0: Security Operations (28%)
Domain 5.0: Security Program Management and Oversight (20%)

steps.title: Applied Cryptography & Mathematical Foundations
steps.goal: Deep dive into cryptographic algorithms, hashing mechanisms, public key infrastructure (PKI), and TLS handshakes.
checklist: Understand symmetric encryption algorithms (AES-GCM, ChaCha20) vs asymmetric (RSA, ECC)
Explain cryptographic hash properties (pre-image resistance, collision resistance, SHA-256)
Trace how digital certificates validate identity through Certificate Authorities (CAs)
Identify legacy weak ciphers (MD5, SHA-1, DES) that must be avoided in modern environments

steps.title: Exam Readiness & Objective Checklist
steps.goal: Systematically review every objective in the official CompTIA SY0-701 exam outline and complete practice test drills.
checklist: Download and audit the official CompTIA SY0-701 objectives PDF line by line
Practice performance-based questions (PBQs) such as configuring firewall ACLs and identifying attack indicators
Achieve consistent 85%+ scores on reputable domain practice tests before scheduling exam

title: Path C — Ethical Hacking & Practical Pentesting
subtitle: Network Exploitation, CTF Problem Solving & Privilege Escalation
description: Hands-on penetration testing methodology, active reconnaissance, initial compromise, privilege escalation, and CTF challenges in legal sandbox environments.
prerequisites: Strong command of Linux command line and TCP/IP networking
legalReminder: Strict Legal Rule: Only test systems you own or have explicit, prior written permission to test. Unauthorized access is strictly illegal under applicable national and international cyber laws. Always require explicit prior written authorization.

steps.title: Practical Network Penetration Testing
steps.goal: Learn end-to-end ethical hacking methodology: passive and active reconnaissance, port scanning, vulnerability scanning, and initial exploitation.
checklist: Conduct legal reconnaissance using Nmap, WHOIS, and DNS enumeration tools
Perform service fingerprinting and vulnerability cross-referencing
Use Metasploit and manual exploit scripts in controlled lab virtual machines
Practice documenting technical findings with reproduction steps and remediation

steps.title: Hands-on CTF Problem Solving (picoCTF)
steps.goal: Develop versatile problem-solving and forensic analysis skills through competition-grade CTF challenges.
checklist: Solve beginner web exploitation challenges (cookie manipulation, client-side validation bypass)
Inspect file headers, metadata, and strings in basic forensics challenges
Decrypt basic classical and modern cipher challenges
Submit verified flags on picoCTF platform independently

steps.title: Linux Target Exploitation & Privilege Escalation (Hack The Box)
steps.goal: Analyze real-world Linux server vulnerabilities, credential harvesting, SUID misconfigurations, and root privilege escalation.
checklist: Follow along and understand IppSec walkthrough methodology for easy Linux boxes
Identify privilege escalation vectors: sudo rights, cron jobs, SUID binaries, kernel exploits
Spawn stable interactive TTY shells from reverse shells
Root at least 5 retired Linux machines on Hack The Box or TryHackMe independently

title: Path D — Web Application Security
subtitle: Lab-First Web Exploitation & OWASP Top 10
description: Lab-first deep dive into modern web application security. Intercept traffic with proxy tools, analyze injection flaws, test access control weaknesses, and master secure coding mitigations.
prerequisites: Basic understanding of HTML, JavaScript, HTTP request/response lifecycles, and relational databases

steps.title: Web Security Academy Interactive Labs
steps.goal: Work through hands-on browser labs covering SQL Injection, XSS, CSRF, and Broken Access Controls.
checklist: Configure Burp Suite Community as an intercepting HTTP/S proxy in your browser
Exploit SQL Injection to retrieve hidden data, bypass login, and query database schemas
Execute Reflected, Stored, and DOM-based Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) proof-of-concepts
Solve at least 20 apprentice and practitioner labs on PortSwigger Web Security Academy

steps.title: Local Vulnerable Application Testing (OWASP Juice Shop)
steps.goal: Run a self-contained vulnerable modern Single Page Application (Node.js/Angular) locally via Docker.
checklist: Deploy OWASP Juice Shop using Docker or local Node.js environment
Inspect client-side JavaScript bundles to identify hidden API routes and sensitive strings
Exploit IDOR (Insecure Direct Object References) and broken access control endpoints
Solve 10+ challenges tracked in the Juice Shop scoreboard

steps.title: Classic PHP/MySQL Vulnerabilities (DVWA)
steps.goal: Compare security levels (Low, Medium, High, Impossible) to understand vulnerability root cause and developer remediation.
checklist: Deploy DVWA locally in an isolated Docker container
Test Command Injection and File Inclusion (LFI/RFI) on Low and Medium security levels
Review the PHP source code for the 'Impossible' level to analyze the defensive patch
Write a brief summary of how parameterized queries prevent SQL injection

steps.title: Web App Sec Video Curriculum
steps.goal: Study systematic web testing workflows and vulnerability discovery techniques.
steps.specialNote: HackerSploit Channel inactive since 2025. Verify commands against current tool documentation.
checklist: Understand directory brute-forcing with Gobuster / ffuf
Analyze HTTP response security headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options)
Document discovered web vulnerabilities with CVSS severity scoring

tracks.title: SOC, SIEM & Incident Response
tracks.summary: Blue-team operations, security telemetry aggregation, SIEM query authoring (Splunk, Elastic, Sentinel), and real-time alert triage.
tracks.suggestAction: Suggest an open-access SIEM course or walkthrough

tracks.title: Cloud Security (AWS, Azure & GCP)
tracks.summary: Identity and Access Management (IAM), least-privilege cloud governance, secure infrastructure-as-code, and cloud security posture management.
tracks.suggestAction: Suggest an open-access cloud security series

tracks.title: AI & LLM Application Security
tracks.summary: Securing generative AI and LLM workflows against prompt injection, insecure output handling, training data poisoning, and unauthorized tool calling.
tracks.suggestAction: Suggest an open-access AI security resource

tracks.title: Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC)
tracks.summary: Enterprise risk modeling, audit readiness (SOC 2, ISO 27001), regulatory compliance (GDPR, HIPAA), and third-party vendor risk assessment.
tracks.suggestAction: Suggest an open-access GRC framework course

tracks.title: Digital Forensics & Incident Response (DFIR)
tracks.summary: Evidence acquisition, memory forensics with Volatility, filesystem timeline reconstruction, and root-cause breach investigation.

tracks.title: Malware Analysis & Reverse Engineering
tracks.summary: Static and dynamic analysis of compiled executables, assembly debugging with Ghidra/x64dbg, and behavioral sandbox inspection.
tracks.suggestAction: Suggest an open-access reverse engineering resource
